title: Shortest Uncommon Substring in an Array
summary: Given an array of non-empty strings, determine for each string the shortest substring that does not appear in any other string in the array.
statement: Given an array of non-empty strings, determine for each string the shortest substring that does not appear in any other string in the array. If there are multiple such substrings, choose the lexicographically smallest. If no such substring exists, return an empty string for that position.
constraints: For each string, find a substring absent from every other array element.
Choose minimum length first and lexicographically smallest second; use an empty string when no candidate exists.
hints: A candidate belongs to one string only when no other full string contains it anywhere.
Enumerate candidate lengths from shortest to longest; collect unique substrings at that length and choose the lexicographic minimum.
For each word and length, test every slice against all other words; stop after the first nonempty candidate set.
Length order proves minimality, the minimum of the first qualifying set enforces the tie rule, and exhaustive slices ensure no candidate is missed.
editorial: Length order proves minimality, the minimum of the first qualifying set enforces the tie rule, and exhaustive slices ensure no candidate is missed.

tests.explanation: For cab the shortest unique choice is ab; bad chooses ba; the other two have no unique substring.
The unique one-letter substrings are a for abc and d for bcd; every substring of abcd appears in another word, so its result is empty.
